guard: a refused operator call to an endpoint other than the manager names the paired caller file that makes it, issued for the space the call resolved and any --server it was given, and endpoint init's Next names the contract it created, quoted for a shell
why: The operator instrument holds request rows for the manager only, so the broker refuses its call to any other endpoint. A refusal with no next step leaves the operator holding a credential whose whoami reads capabilities: all.

An auth mint resolves its own target, so an issuance without --space signs for the current space rather than the one that refused. The remedy carries the resolved space and an explicit --server, each quoted for a shell when it needs to be.
The init scaffold knows the directory it created, so a placeholder in its Next is a step the operator has to rewrite by hand.
The suite imports the CLI source and runs endpoint init in process, so no mutation needs a build.
